items.subject: QR
items.prompt: A rectangle is 5 inches long and 3 inches wide. If its width is doubled and its length stays the same, how many times as large is the new area?
items.explanation: The old area is 5 × 3 = 15. The new area is 5 × 6 = 30. 30 is 2 times 15. Doubling one side doubles the area.
items.misconceptions: doubles both sides; answers a length

why.B: 4 is what happens when BOTH sides are doubled. Here only the width changes.
why.C: 6 is the new width. The question asks how many times the area grows.
why.D: 8 adds the two sides of the original rectangle (5 + 3) and does not compare areas.

items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: A square has sides 4 centimeters long. If every side is doubled, how many times as large is the new area?
items.explanation: The old area is 4 × 4 = 16. The new square has sides of 8, so its area is 8 × 8 = 64. 64 ÷ 16 = 4.
items.misconceptions: treats doubling both sides like doubling one

why.A: 2 would be right if only one side were doubled. Both the length and the width double, so the area doubles twice.
why.C: 8 is the new side length, not how many times the area grows.
why.D: 16 is the old area (4 × 4), not how many times the area grows.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: A rectangle is 7 meters long and 2 meters wide. Its length is made 3 meters longer. By how many meters does the perimeter increase?
items.explanation: The old perimeter is 2 × (7 + 2) = 18. The new one is 2 × (10 + 2) = 24. 24 − 18 = 6, because both long sides grew by 3.
items.misconceptions: adds the change to one side only

why.B: 9 adds 3 three times. Only the two long sides change.
why.C: 12 adds 3 to all four sides. The widths stay 2 meters.
why.D: 24 is the new perimeter. The question asks how much it grew: 24 − 18.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: Points A, B, C and D are on a line in that order. AB is 5, BC is 3 and AD is 12. What is the length of CD?
items.explanation: AD is the whole line: AB + BC + CD = 12. So 5 + 3 + CD = 12, and CD = 4.
items.misconceptions: forgets a piece; adds a length that is already inside another

why.B: 7 is 12 − 5, the length of BD. BC is part of BD, so take it away too.
why.D: 20 adds all three lengths. AD already includes AB and BC.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: Points A, B, C and D are on a line in that order. AC is 10, BD is 9 and BC is 4. What is the length of AD?
items.explanation: AC and BD overlap on BC. AC + BD = 19 counts BC twice, so take it away once: 19 − 4 = 15. (Or: AB = 10 − 4 = 6, CD = 9 − 4 = 5, and 6 + 4 + 5 = 15.)
items.misconceptions: counts the overlap twice

why.A: 5 is CD alone (9 − 4). AD runs all the way from A to D.
why.B: 6 is AB alone (10 − 4). AD runs all the way from A to D.
why.C: 13 adds BD and BC (9 + 4), counting BC twice and leaving out AB.

items.subject: QR
items.subskill: counting a group with an overlap
items.prompt: In a class, 18 students like soccer and 12 like basketball. Five of them like both. How many students like at least one of the two sports?
items.explanation: 18 + 12 = 30 counts the 5 who like both twice. Take them away once: 30 − 5 = 25.
items.misconceptions: counts the overlap twice

why.A: 5 is only the students who like both sports.
why.B: 7 is the students who like basketball only (12 − 5).
why.C: 13 is the students who like soccer only (18 − 5).

items.subject: QR
items.subskill: how many are in neither group
items.prompt: There are 28 students in a class. Fifteen have a dog, 9 have a cat, and 4 have both. How many students have neither a dog nor a cat?
items.explanation: Students with a pet: 15 + 9 − 4 = 20 (the 4 were counted in both groups). Students without: 28 − 20 = 8.
items.misconceptions: counts the overlap twice; answers the wrong group

why.A: 4 takes 15 + 9 = 24 away from 28, but the 4 with both pets were counted twice in the 24.
why.C: 20 is the students who have at least one pet (15 + 9 − 4). The question asks about the others.
why.D: 24 adds 15 and 9, counting the 4 with both pets twice, and it is not the number without pets.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: If 3 × □ + 4 = 19, what number goes in the box?
items.explanation: Undo the steps in reverse: 19 − 4 = 15, then 15 ÷ 3 = 5. Check: 3 × 5 + 4 = 19.
items.misconceptions: stops halfway; undoes with the wrong operation

why.B: 15 is 19 − 4, which is 3 × □. Divide by 3 to find □.
why.D: 57 multiplies 19 by 3. Undo × 3 by dividing.

items.subject: QR
items.subskill: a term far along a pattern
items.prompt: The pattern 3, 7, 11, 15, … adds 4 each time. What is the 10th number in the pattern?
items.explanation: From the 1st number to the 10th there are 9 steps of 4. 3 + 9 × 4 = 3 + 36 = 39.
items.misconceptions: counts one step too many or too few

why.A: 31 is the 8th number. Count the terms: the 10th is two more steps.
why.B: 35 is the 9th number. Count the terms: the 10th is one more step.
why.C: 36 is 9 × 4, the nine steps without the 3 the pattern starts at.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: A 12-ounce bottle of juice costs $3.00. What is the cost per ounce?
items.misconceptions: divides the wrong way

why.B: $0.36 multiplies 3 by 12 instead of dividing. Share $3.00 among 12 ounces.
why.D: $4.00 is 12 ÷ 3, the division the wrong way round. One ounce cannot cost more than the bottle.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: A bag has 3 red marbles for every 5 blue marbles. There are 40 marbles in all. How many are red?
items.explanation: Each group of 3 red and 5 blue holds 8 marbles. 40 ÷ 8 = 5 groups. Red: 5 × 3 = 15.
items.misconceptions: mixes up the size of a group with the number of groups

why.A: 8 is the number of marbles in one group of 3 red and 5 blue.
why.C: 24 is 3 × 8. There are 5 groups of 8, so red is 3 × 5.
why.D: 25 is the number of blue marbles.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: Ana scored 80, 90, 70 and 100 on four quizzes. What is her average score?
items.misconceptions: stops at the total

why.A: 80 is the first score. Add all four and share them out.
why.C: 90 is one of her scores. The mean is the total divided by 4.
why.D: 340 is the total. Divide it by 4 to find the average.

items.subject: QR
items.subskill: which number leaves a given remainder
items.prompt: When a number is divided by 5, the remainder is 3. Which could be the number?
items.explanation: A number that leaves 3 when divided by 5 ends in 3 or 8. 28 = 5 × 5 + 3.
items.misconceptions: confuses remainder with a digit

why.D: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 with no remainder. It ends in 5, not 3 or 8.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: The letter n stands for an odd number. Which expression must be even?
items.explanation: Try n = 5: n + 1 = 6, which is even. Adding 1 to any odd number reaches the next even number.
items.misconceptions: adds an even amount and expects the parity to change

why.A: 3 times an odd number is odd: 3 × 5 = 15.
why.C: An odd number plus 2 is the next odd number: 5 + 2 = 7.
why.D: 2n is even, and one more than an even number is odd.

items.prompt: What number is 1,000 more than 49,650?

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: A movie starts at 6:45 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 50 minutes. When does it end?
items.explanation: 6:45 + 1 hour = 7:45. Then 50 more minutes: 15 minutes reaches 8:00, and 35 more makes 8:35 p.m.
items.misconceptions: adds only the minutes; rounds the time

why.A: 7:35 p.m. adds only the 50 minutes, not the hour.
why.D: 8:45 p.m. adds 2 whole hours, 10 minutes too many.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: A rope 3 yards long is cut into pieces that are each 1 foot long. How many pieces are there?
items.explanation: One yard is 3 feet, so 3 yards are 3 × 3 = 9 feet. That makes 9 one-foot pieces.
items.misconceptions: uses the wrong conversion

why.A: 3 counts yards, not feet. Each yard is 3 feet.
why.C: 12 uses 4 feet in a yard. A yard is 3 feet.
why.D: 36 is the number of inches in a yard.

items.subject: QR
items.subskill: perimeter from area and one side
items.prompt: A rectangle has an area of 24 square feet and a length of 6 feet. What is its perimeter?
items.explanation: Width = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 feet. Perimeter = 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 feet.
items.misconceptions: stops at the width; mixes up area and perimeter

why.A: 4 feet is the width (24 ÷ 6). The question asks for the perimeter.
why.B: 10 feet adds the length and the width once. A rectangle has two of each.
why.D: 24 is the area. Perimeter is the distance around.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: Jon read 2/5 of a book on Monday and 1/3 of it on Tuesday. What fraction of the book does he still have to read?
items.explanation: Use fifteenths: 2/5 = 6/15 and 1/3 = 5/15. He has read 11/15, so 15/15 − 11/15 = 4/15 is left.
items.misconceptions: stops at the part read; adds tops and bottoms

why.A: 1/15 is 2/5 − 1/3, the difference between the two days. The question asks what is left of the whole book.
why.C: 5/8 adds the tops and bottoms (2 + 1 over 5 + 3) and takes that from 1.
why.D: 11/15 is how much he has read. Take it away from 1.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: The mean of five numbers is 6. Four of the numbers are 4, 5, 7 and 8. What is the fifth number?
items.explanation: A mean of 6 for 5 numbers means a total of 5 × 6 = 30. 4 + 5 + 7 + 8 = 24, so the fifth number is 30 − 24 = 6.
items.misconceptions: stops at a total

why.B: 8 is the largest of the four numbers given, not the missing one.
why.C: 24 is the total of the four numbers given. The five numbers must total 30.
why.D: 30 is the total of all five. Take away the four you know.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: The point (3, 5) is moved 4 units right and 2 units down. Where is it now?
items.explanation: Right 4 adds 4 to the first number: 3 + 4 = 7. Down 2 takes 2 from the second: 5 − 2 = 3. The point is (7, 3).
items.misconceptions: moves the wrong way; swaps the moves

why.A: (1, 7) moves left 2 and up 2: the wrong way both times, and only 2 across instead of 4.
why.B: (5, 9) moves the first number by 2 and the second by 4, and goes up: the moves are swapped.
why.D: (7, 7) moves up 2 instead of down 2.

items.subject: QR
items.subskill: chance of not picking a color
items.prompt: A bag holds 3 red, 6 blue and 1 green marble. One marble is picked without looking. What is the chance it is NOT blue?
items.explanation: There are 3 + 6 + 1 = 10 marbles. Not blue means red or green: 3 + 1 = 4. The chance is 4 out of 10.
items.misconceptions: answers the opposite event; counts only one color

why.A: 1 out of 10 is the chance of green only. Red is not blue either.
why.B: 3 out of 10 is the chance of red only. Green is not blue either.
why.D: 6 out of 10 is the chance it IS blue.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: Every student in Ms. Ray's class plays an instrument. Ben does not play an instrument. Which statement must be true?

choices.B: Ben is in Ms. Ray's class.
choices.C: Ben is not in Ms. Ray's class.
choices.D: Some of Ms. Ray's students do not play.

items.explanation: Everyone in the class plays. Ben does not play. So Ben cannot be in the class.
items.misconceptions: brings in something not stated; contradicts a fact

why.A: Nothing in the facts mentions sports.
why.B: If he were, he would play an instrument, and he does not.
why.D: The first fact says every student in the class plays.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: Which is closest to 49 × 51?
items.explanation: Both numbers are close to 50, and 50 × 50 = 2,500. (The exact answer is 2,499.)
items.misconceptions: loses or adds a zero

why.B: 2,000 rounds 49 and 51 to 40 and 50, but both are close to 50.
why.C: 2,450 is 49 × 50. The other number is 51, one more than 50, which adds about 49 more.
